info.name: Bifrost V1 - Extra Fields Placement
info.description: client.extra_fields_placement end to end, streaming and non-streaming. Body mode (the default) keeps the extra_fields object in JSON bodies and SSE chunks and adds no new headers. Headers mode removes extra_fields from every body, every SSE chunk and error bodies, and carries the routed identity and scalar fields as x-bifrost-* response headers: native /v1/chat/completions and /v1/responses, and the /openai integration, each unary and streaming, plus a provider error. Streams carry only what is known before the first chunk (routing identity, request type, cache lookup), so the stream checks assert those headers and not latency. A cross-origin request checks Access-Control-Expose-Headers lists the x-bifrost-* headers so browsers can read them. The routing identity headers that existed before this setting (x-bifrost-provider, original and resolved model, request type, fallback index and every x-bifrost-routing-info-*) are pinned so the setting cannot regress them: in body mode they must equal the matching extra_fields values, and the same unary, streaming and fallback requests must produce the same values in headers mode. Setup snapshots client_config and Teardown restores it verbatim. Known limit: a fresh install reads back log_retention_days 0, which PUT /api/config refuses, so the snapshot raises it to 30. Setup fails if placement is not body when the run starts (a killed earlier run can leave headers mode behind), and Teardown always restores body; the runner also restores the placement it found if newman stops early.

item.name: Responses streaming keeps one top-level extra_fields per event

exec: pm.test('Responses streaming returns 200', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code, 'body: ' + pm.response.text()).to.equal(200); });
pm.test('the stream delivered SSE chunks', function () { var t = pm.response.text(); pm.expect(t, t).to.include('data: '); pm.expect(t, t).to.include('response.completed'); });
var events = pm.response.text().split('\n').filter(function (l) { return l.indexOf('data: ') === 0 && l !== 'data: [DONE]'; }).map(function (l) { return JSON.parse(l.slice(6)); });

pm.test('every event carries a top-level extra_fields', function () { pm.expect(events.length, pm.response.text()).to.be.above(0); events.forEach(function (e) { pm.expect(e.extra_fields, JSON.stringify(e)).to.be.an('object'); }); });

pm.test('no lifecycle event nests extra_fields in its response', function () { var lifecycle = events.filter(function (e) { return e.response; }); pm.expect(lifecycle.length, pm.response.text()).to.be.above(0); lifecycle.forEach(function (e) { pm.expect(e.response, JSON.stringify(e)).to.not.have.property('extra_fields'); }); });

pm.test('body mode adds no x-bifrost-latency-ms header', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('x-bifrost-latency-ms'), 'headers: ' + JSON.stringify(pm.response.headers.toObject())).to.be.oneOf([undefined, null]); });
